messages.content:
Question: Which type of adversarial example generation method results in images that are visually more similar to the original images?
Evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 3, page 8) (image attached): Figure 3: The normal test images are termed as Normal , and adversarial examples generated on Resnet-32 (CE) and Resnet-32 (RCE) are separately termed as CE / RCE . Adversarial examples are generated by C&W-wb with minimal distortions.
Words printed in the figure: MNIST Normal CE RCE CIFAR-10
[E2] (figure, Figure 3, page 8): a zoomed view of Figure 3 (image attached) [image]

claims.text: Adversarial examples are generated by C&W-wb with minimal distortions.

cites.quote: Adversarial examples are generated by C&W-wb with minimal distortions.

claims.text: Based on the visual comparison, adversarial examples generated on Resnet-32 (CE) termed as CE show images that are visually more similar to the original normal test images compared to Resnet-32 (RCE) termed as RCE.

cites.quote: The normal test images are termed as Normal , and adversarial examples generated on Resnet-32 (CE) and Resnet-32 (RCE) are separately termed as CE / RCE .

cites.observation: In the image, the CE row of adversarial examples for both MNIST and CIFAR-10 closely resembles the Normal row, whereas the RCE row contains significantly more visible noise and distortion.
